tools.name: render_document
tools.title: Render a document
tools.description: Convert Markdown, LaTeX or a texwright JSON document to PDF, HTML or JSON and write it to a file in the workspace. LaTeX math, numbered equations/figures/tables, cross-references (@fig:x, \ref{}), citations ([@key], \cite{}) and a table of contents are supported. Returns the output path and diagnostics; when ok is false, fix the reported lines and call again. Call get_guide once for the syntax.

path.description: Path of a .md, .tex or .json file inside the workspace. Give this or `source`.

format.description: Input format; inferred from the path extension, default markdown

base_dir.description: Folder inside the workspace that images, \input files and bibliographies resolve against when using `source`

bibliography.description: Bibliography files (.bib or CSL-JSON), relative to the document

compact.description: Return diagnostics as one line each (file:line:col severity code message | hint | fix) to save tokens

output_path.description: Where to write the result, inside the workspace; default next to `path`, or a fresh temporary folder for `source`

max_pages.description: Tighten margins, then the body size, until the PDF fits in this many pages

tools.name: preview_page
tools.title: Look at pages
tools.description: Typeset the document exactly as the PDF would be and return pages as PNG images, so you can see the result: layout, figures, tables, math, what overflows. Also returns the page count and the page each heading, figure, table and numbered equation landed on, to decide which pages to look at. `pages` defaults to [1], at most 4 per call; `dpi` defaults to 100 (a letter page is then 850 x 1100 pixels).

tools.name: check_document
tools.title: Check a document
tools.description: Validate a document without rendering: parses it, numbers everything, typesets every formula, resolves references, citations and images. Returns diagnostics with stable codes, line, column and a hint; many carry a `fix` ({line, col, old, new, safe}) you can apply as an edit. Fast; use it after every edit.

tools.name: fix_document
tools.title: Apply safe fixes
tools.description: Check the file at `path`, apply every safe fix (typos in labels, keys, commands and image names; missing closers; broken front matter) to it and the files it includes, and check again. Returns the fixes written and the remaining diagnostics. Writes files in the workspace.

tools.name: repair_document
tools.title: Repair and render
tools.description: One call for the whole fix loop: check the file at `path`, apply every safe fix (typos in labels, keys, commands, environment and image names and option values; missing } \right \end{...}; broken front matter) until nothing more applies, taking back any round that makes it worse, then render it when no errors are left. Returns what was fixed (line, old -> new), what is left (each with a hint and, where known, a fix marked safe or not: apply the unsafe ones after a look), the output path, page count and where headings, figures and tables landed. With `compact` (default true) the report is a few short text lines. Writes the file and the output in the workspace.

tools.name: outline_document
tools.title: Outline a document
tools.description: What is where in a document, without reading all of it: headings, figures, tables, equations, theorems and listings in order, with numbers, labels, source lines and how often each is referenced, plus cited keys and a word count. Use it to navigate long documents and to find unreferenced figures or tables.

tools.description: How to write documents for texwright: Markdown and LaTeX syntax, math, references, citations, figures, tables, layout keys, diagnostics and the fix-and-retry workflow. Pass short: true for a one-page cheat sheet.

short.description: The one-page cheat sheet instead of the full guide

tools.name: new_document
tools.title: Start from a template
tools.description: A complete, valid starter document to fill in. Kinds: paper (Research paper: abstract, numbered sections, equations, theorem and proof, results table, citations); report (Report: summary first, findings with a table, footnote, callout, recommendations, contents); homework (Problem set solutions: unnumbered problems, derivations, an induction proof, matrices); notes (Lecture notes: definitions, lemmas, theorems with proofs, examples, exercises); cv (One-page résumé (max-pages: 1, compact theme)); letter (Formal letter on one page: addresses, subject line, body, closing); memo (Decision memo: header table, decision needed, options table, next steps); proposal (Project proposal: problem, solution, timeline and budget tables, measures, risks). With `path`, writes it (and any files it uses, such as refs.bib) into the workspace; existing files are not overwritten.

path.description: Where to write the document inside the workspace, e.g. report.md
